meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (national jurisdiction, unitary; no sub-state corporate registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law tradition with significant Common Law-influenced corporate statutes (Law 32 of 1927) and an independent Financial Center regulatory overlay
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United Kingdom-Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1985)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT regime; establishes Unidad de Análisis Financiero as the FIU and Intendencia de Sujetos No Financieros as DNFBP supervisor); Law 70 of 30 October 2019 (Transparency and Ultimate Beneficial Owner Registry - Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiario Final, RTBF); Executive Decree No. 36 of 26 January 2022 (RTBF implementing regulation); Law 32 of 1927 (Sociedad Anónima formation; resident agent and statutory minimum requirements); Commercial Code and Registro Público tariffs.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the origin country is a Hague Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization through the competent Panamanian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or utility provider in the ultimate beneficial owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter covering the source of funds and payment rails for the proposed video-match application
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depository financial institution of the contributing shareholder / ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Security-attested or notarized signature followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, plus sworn Spanish translation by Panamanian translator if issued in non-Spanish script

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn statement of source of wealth and source of funds for the intended initial capitalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the ultimate beneficial owner's residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed shareholders, directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against: (i) OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN); (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database; (iv) FATF public statements and grey-list monitoring; (v) Panama's domestic sanctions and alerts published by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero; and (vi) adverse media / Politically Exposed Persons indicators, applying Law 23 of 2015 enhanced due diligence standards for PEPs, non-face-to-face customers, medium-risk digital payment businesses, and cash-exposed foreign ownership structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección General del Registro Público (www.registropublico.gob.pa); online reservation channel 'Portal de Servicios en Línea' and physical counter at the Sede de Panamá for certified certificate issuance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in Spanish or any Roman-alphabet language; non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into a Roman-alphabet version in the articles of incorporation and public registry entry; every corporate name must carry a mandatory S.A., Corp., Inc., or equivalent suffix denoting limited liability status; the Registro Público applies a phonetic and visual similarity doctrine in Spanish transliteration, distinguishing only diacritical marks, spaces, and punctuation is insufficient to avoid confusion.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: PANAMA / PANAMÁ or derivations suggesting state sponsorship
BANCO / BANK / FINANCIERA / CRÉDITO without prior license of the Superintendencia de Bancos
SEGUROS / REASEGUROS / CORREDOR DE SEGUROS without prior license of the Superintendencia de Seguros
BOLSA / MERCADO DE VALORES / FONDO DE INVERSIÓN without prior license of the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores
OFICIAL / NACIONAL / GOBIERNO / MINISTERIO implying public authority or official endorsement
FIDUCIARIO / FIDEICOMISO / TRUST implying licensed fiduciary activity
TOURISM-CASINO / APUESTA / LUDOPATÍA tokens restricted by the Junta de Control de Juegos
any identical or confusingly similar name to an existing registered company in the Public Registry database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon registry rejection, the resident agent shall within five business days file an 'Escrito de Reconsideración' before the Dirección General del Registro Público, attaching the negative search certificate, the proposed Spanish/Roman transliteration, and a concise memorandum demonstrating non-confusion and compliance with name suffix rules; if the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a contentious-administrative action before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within the statutory limitation period; simultaneously, a new alternative name may be reserved to avoid transactional delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office for a Panama Sociedad Anónima. Law 32 of 1927 and registral practice require the resident agent to maintain a physical office in Panama capable of receiving original documents and service of process. However, for this digital video-matching business with no physical Panama presence, a virtual office for correspondence is contractually acceptable under the resident-agent service arrangement, provided the registered address disclosed to merchants is the resident agent's physical address; this does not, by itself, constitute illegal 'registered office farming'.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For the S.A. itself: Low (approximately 4-6% annualized) given the absence of physical premises, non-resident ownership, and the medium-risk digital services profile; for the resident agent: moderate (approximately 20-30% annualized) because the Intendencia de Sujetos No Financieros conducts thematic on-site AML/CFT inspections; additionally, banking and payment-rail acquirers such as Paymentwall and Apple IAP may perform non-onsite KYC verification including recorded video calls, virtual site visits, and IP-geolocation checks, substituting for physical inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (as amended by Ley 5 de 1993) — Sociedades Anónimas; codified under the Registro Público regulations, Title I (Articles 1–40), covering execution, inscription, and governance of the corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública (Public Deed) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorized capital may be nominal (e.g., USD 10,000) with no escrow, deposit, or bank-account funding requirement prior to incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE INCORPORATING SHAREHOLDERS AND FIRST DIRECTORS OF [●], S.A. WHEREAS the Corporation was validly incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Panama; RESOLVED: the issuance, subscription and allotment of the authorized capital shares to the initial subscriber is approved, reflected in the corporate ledger as subscribed capital; RESOLVED: the registered office is established at the offices of the registered agent, [●], situated in Panama City, Republic of Panama, and such office is adopted for receipt of legal notices; RESOLVED: the following officers are appointed for the first term: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each empowered to execute bank accounts, contracts, and platform filings; RESOLVED: the payment of all incorporation fees and the execution of ancillary documents by the registered agent are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Nombre (via SERTRADEN online portal or physical counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name-search application (Solicitud de Búsqueda de Nombre) in the registrant's name or via a Panamanian attorney; the registry verifies that the proposed name (e.g., 'VideoMatch, S.A.') is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company; upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days and the certificado de búsqueda is issued.
required_dossiers: Solicitud de Búsqueda de Nombre (signed application)
Copy of passport of the incorporating shareholder
Power of attorney if filed through a registered attorney
Description of the corporate purpose (ISIC 6311 digital platform services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the name due to similarity, promptly file an auxiliary search listing three alternative names (primera, segunda, tercera opción) and pay the minor re-search fee to obtain a new reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarized Execution of the Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (Panamanian Notary Public of the Circuit, Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator executes the Escritura Pública containing the articles of incorporation: corporate name, registered agent, authorized capital, share classes (registered or bearer), corporate purpose limited to lawful digital services, and first director appointments. If the incorporator is abroad, execution is made through a duly notarized and apostilled power of attorney held by the Panamanian attorney.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation approved by the incorporator
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney (if executing by attorney)
Passport copies of incorporators and first directors
Registered agent acceptance letter
Valid name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects, revise the deed clauses and hold a supplementary notarial hearing to re-execute the corrected Escritura Pública before any registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Fees and Fiscal Stamps
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Treasury/Cashier (Caja) and Banco Nacional de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After execution of the deed, pay the official registration fee (based on the authorized capital), the stamp tax on issuance of shares, and the nominal incorporation tax (Tasa). The cashier issues a stamped payment receipt which must be attached to the deed before the inscription application is accepted.
required_dossiers: Testimonio (original certified copy) of the Public Deed
Payment voucher for registration fees and stamps
Name search certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fees are underpaid or the tariff code is misapplied, issue a supplemental payment (complemento de pago) at the same cashier and attach the new receipt to the original dossier within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Public Deed in the Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the testimonio along with all payment receipts at the registry's submission desk. The registrar performs a legal review (calificación registrar) and, upon approval, assigns a Folio Real number and records the corporation in the mercantile register.
required_dossiers: Original testimonio of the Escritura Pública
Original stamped government payment receipts
Three additional certified copies for registry stamping
Completed registry cover form (carátula de inscripción)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'calificación defectuosa' or clarification memo, file a corrective Escritura de Aclaración within thirty days; alternatively, request provisional annotation (anotación provisional) to protect priority pending correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Corporate Certificate and Opening of Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certification Desk and the Registered Agent's Corporate Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful inscription, request the Certificado de Personería Jurídica and certified copies of the registered deed. Concurrently, open the corporate books: share ledger (Libro de Acciones), minutes book (Libro de Actas), and register the officers in the corresponding internal record to evidence good standing.
required_dossiers: Inscription reference number (Folio Real)
Written application for Certificado de Personería Jurídica
Payment of certificate issuance fee
Attorney's identification and request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed, file a written diligence at the registry's Mesa de Salida; for urgent closing deadlines, use the express service (servicio urgente) with supplementary fee and obtain the certificate the same day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Industrias; no industrial/manufacturing license applicable to ISIC 6311 digital OTT platform
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory industrial operating permit required for pure data-processing, hosting, or video-match software services under Panamanian law

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA — Category 0/Exempt because the entity operates a remote digital platform with no physical industrial facility, construction, or pollutant-emitting installation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation; any incidental office waste must comply with municipal solid-waste collection ordinances; if leased office HVAC is installed, applicable refrigerant leakage standards under MiAMBIENTE Resolution AG-0440 shall be respected

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety annual inspection by Dirección de Bomberos de Panamá for any leased commercial office; workplace health clearance from Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) covering employee sanitation; occupational health and social security registration with CSS/MITRADEL for local staff; building structural-load and occupancy certificates required only for high-rise office leases

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; online services portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panama S.A. (PA_CORP), the statutory TIN is the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), issued by the DGI. A company must first obtain registered articles / aviso de operación from the Public Registry of Panama. The legal representative or resident fiscal agent must then submit to DGI: (i) notarized RUC registration form; (ii) certified copy of the public deed and articles of incorporation; (iii) copy of the mercantile registry inscription (Ficha/Inscripción); (iv) identity documents (CED/PASSPORT) of directors, officers and resident agent; and (v) evidence of the Panamanian registered office address. DGI assigns the permanent RUC and, where required, activates the ITBMS/VAT ID. A foreign entity without a Panama branch that undertakes taxable activities in Panama registers through an appointed fiscal representative under the same procedure. PA_CORP must keep the RUC active and file zero returns where no Panama-source taxable activity is generated, although foreign-source income remains outside Panama's territorial tax charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (Entity_Level_Taxation): a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima is a separate juridical person automatically taxed at entity level; only Panama-source income is assessable, foreign-source income is exempt, and there is no pass-through/transparent status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None equivalent to a U.S. check-the-box or OECD hybrid-mismatch election. Panamanian law mandates entity-level taxation of a S.A.; no classification election is available between corporate and pass-through status. Administrative elections limited to accounting basis (accrual/cash where permitted), voluntary ITBMS registration, small-taxpayer simplified regime, and territorial-source apportionment methods for mixed activities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (ITBMS — Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y la Prestación de Servicios)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 - no general economic threshold; every person habitually engaged in taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama must register with DGI before operating. Occasional non-business transfers are outside the regime. A DGI-designated small-taxpayer simplified regime may reduce compliance obligations for low-turnover traders, but does not eliminate the RUC/ITBMS registration duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All DGI-registered taxpayers designated for online invoicing must issue digital invoices through approved or DGI-hosted software in the SIFE (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica) environment. Invoices must be submitted to DGI through its web-services/API in real time or near-real time and incorporate a DGI-assigned acceptance code, electronic control stamp and QR/fiscal hash. The DGI may validate/censure invoice series before and after issuance; failure to transmit transactional data through the API is treated as non-issued tax documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: zero-rated ITBMS only when the goods are physically exported from Panama under a valid customs export declaration and the sale is to a non-resident customer. For services (including real-time video matching and cross-border social telephony): zero-rating applies where the recipient is not resident in Panama and the service is economically consumed/used outside Panama. PA_CORP must maintain per-transaction evidence that the user/subscriber is non-resident and that the digital service is not enjoyed in Panama; Apple_IAP and Paymentwall settlement reports and IP/geolocation logs are acceptable corroboration. If a Panamanian consumer obtains the service or payment is received with a Panama card/IP, the 7% local ITBMS must be collected, even if the platform is foreign-incorporated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) - applicable to physical goods only; not applicable to pure digital video-match services
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill - applicable to physical goods export only; not used for offshore services
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank settlement statement evidencing the amount paid by the non-resident customer and credited to a Panamanian account
Apple IAP and Paymentwall payout statements, service contracts, user terms, and IP-geolocation evidence demonstrating non-Panamanian counterparty and offshore place of use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may reclassify a claimed zero-rated transaction as taxable at 7% if the export/foreign-use evidence is incomplete or contradictory; assess omitted tax, monthly statutory surcharges and interest; apply fine scales of 50% to 300% of evaded tax; deny or claw back VAT credits and refunds with retrospective effect (generally 5 years, or longer where fraud); and file criminal tax-fraud charges. Directors, the resident agent and signatories are jointly and severally liable for overstated export exemptions or fabricated export documentation, and criminal conviction carries imprisonment of up to 6 years and disqualification from DGI e-invoicing and export facilitation programs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) in coordination with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) act as ancillary supervisory bodies
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system in which the United States dollar is the sole unrestricted legal tender for all obligations; the balboa is merely a coin-denominated unit equal to 1:1 with the USD and is not independently issue-prone. There is no exchange control law, no central bank discount window, and no statutory restriction on current account or capital account convertibility. Repatriation of branch profits or dividends to foreign shareholders is freely permitted via wire transfer in USD, although Panamanian territorial tax rules impose a 5% corporate dividend tax on distributions sourced from Panamanian business profits and a nominal annual registration fee on licensed corporations. The absence of a formal central bank means that foreign exchange rate formation is purely market-driven, and balance-of-payments settlement occurs through the private banking correspondent network in the United States.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement under Panama law to surrender export receipts to any official authority, nor is there a mandatory conversion ratio or time-bound repatriation deadline. Export proceeds may be legitimately retained in USD or foreign currency accounts at authorized Panamanian banks, and the free disposition of export earnings is expressly permitted because the USD is the national legal tender. The only relevant obligations relate to documentary transparency (e.g., customs declarations, invoices, and bill-of-lading records) and to bank record-keeping under Panamanian Law 41 of 2000, as amended, where receipts exceeding US$10,000 trigger customer due diligence and suspicious transaction reporting obligations to the UAF.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border digital EMI banking, including foreign payment e-money institutions such as Airwallex, Meridian, or US-based chartered bank-partner platforms, is viable only as an ancillary treasury rail, rated 'Medium' overall. Panamanian banking law does not formally prohibit the initiation of accounts with non-resident EMIs, and the USD-denominated ecosystem permits direct sweep structures; however, SBP circulars and UAF guidelines impose an 'enhanced due diligence register' for any corporate client using an underlying foreign EMI, requiring proof of EMI licensing in its home jurisdiction, audited financial statements of the EMI, and a written rationale for why a domestic Panamanian bank account is insufficient. Foreign EMI onboarding for the PA_CORP video-match application is further constrained by the enhanced AML risk tier assigned to digital dating and social telephony platforms, making domestic bank sponsorship or a co-account at a Tier-1 Panamanian bank materially more efficient.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under SBP Rule 4-2015 and the Unified Banking Guidelines, at least one director and the designated beneficial owner (natural person owning ≥10%) must undergo an in-person KYC interview at a licensed Panamanian bank's branch or notary office within Panama. Remote opening is generally not permitted for a Sociedad Anónima holding escrow capital, unless the bank has obtained an express waiver from the UAF for a 'qualifying technology client'—which is extremely rare and requires board resolutions, apostilled charter, and a physical visit by a local legal representative. The alternative is a 'semi-remote' flow: directors first appear before a Panama-licensed legal agent who certifies identity, after which the bank accepts couriered documentation, but a mandatory first televised (or in-person) call with a compliance officer remains non-waivable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner residing in a high-risk or uncooperative tax jurisdiction or using a nominee director layer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport of the ultimate beneficial owner, Panamanian legal agent certification of corporate good standing, sworn affidavit of source of funds, and a detailed organizational chart showing the chain of control from the PA_CORP entity to the natural person(s) with 25% or more economic interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-transaction volume of cross-border app payments (video match app) with counterparties in FATF-enhanced jurisdictions and reliance on Apple IAP / Paymentwall as principal payment rails
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements (or reviewed management accounts) for the prior 2 years, platform transaction volume reports, processor settlement statements from Apple and Paymentwall, written KYC/AML policies of the app, and a board resolution designating the treasury controller, accompanied by an internal questionnaire describing the commercial model, expected daily transaction value, and chargeback profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow account credited from an offshore jurisdiction with opaque source of funds or frequent transfers in excess of US$10,000 that trigger mandatory UAF reporting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 from the investing shareholder, certified copy of the capital injection board resolution, purchase agreement or convertible note evidencing arms-length funding, and a legalized certificate of tax residence (or refundable-tax-exemption letter) of the transferring entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export receipts or operating collections routed through a foreign electronic money institution rather than a domestic clearing account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal EMI integration agreement, EMI licensing certificate from a recognized European Union or US state regulator, daily reconciliation ledger between EMI and the Panamanian treasury account, and a legal opinion on the permissibility of EMI sweeps under SBP Rule 4-2015.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital must be injected through the regular SWIFT channel using MT103 from the shareholder's account at a foreign bank to the Panamanian operational or escrow account at a Tier-1 licensed bank. The beneficiary SWIFT/BIC, ABA routing, and account statement should explicitly reference the purpose of the disbursement as 'CAPITAL_CONTRIBUTION' or 'INVESTMENT' using standard banking comment fields, accompanied by a board resolution file in the bank's internal KYC system. While Panama does not assign official customs codes or central-bank purpose codes, UAF-prescribed due diligence requires the bank to write 'REPRESENTATIVE OFFICE FUNDING – VIDEO MATCH PLATFORM' in the instruction; electronic verification can be expedited by issuing a SWIFT MT199 pre-advice from the investor's bank 24 hours before the principal transfer. The full routing path should be optimized through US correspondent banks (e.g., JPMorgan Chase, Citibank, Bank of America) as Panama has no central bank settlement infrastructure, and the transaction should never be segmented to avoid the US$10,000 due-diligence reporting threshold.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements are domestic USD clearings (ACH Panama, operated through the Panamá Clearing House) for local disbursements and SWIFT-based MT103 wire transfers for all cross-border commercial payments. For merchant payouts to licensors, content providers, or technology vendors, the recommended rail is MT103 'for the account' via correspondent U.S. banks with standard ISO 20022 remittance data (payment reference: INVOICE NUMBER; platform transaction ID; ISIC_6311 service descriptor). For larger settlement flows (e.g., ≥US$500,000 or monthly recurring infrastructure licensing), the entity should utilise Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) with confirmed irrevocable undertakings from a Panamanian issuing bank, with documents to include commercial invoice, provider acceptance certificate, and UAF-compliant transaction reports. The treasury policy should restrict manual wire release authority to two directors (dual control) and require SWIFT rejection of any outbound payment to sanctioned entities on the OFAC / UN lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla USD/COP forward contracts with SBP-licensed Panamanian banks or their regional affiliates to hedge Colombian-peso-priced content licensing costs, covered under elective hedge accounting guidance IFRS 9

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with a non-Panamanian global bank under an ISDA Master Agreement for Latin American currencies (e.g., USD/BRL, USD/ARS, USD/PEN) in cases where deliverability is impossible due to local currency restrictions, limited to 12-month tenors

Cross-currency swaps between USD and affiliate functional currencies (EUR, MXN, COP) executed with a rated international bank counterparty, used exclusively to align cash flows from the video-match subscription revenue and international telephony interconnection fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable and due on or before 31 March for each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues moratory interest (≈1% per month) and surcharges, blocks issuance of tax clearance (Paz y Salvo), and two consecutive unpaid years can trigger administrative strike-off by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Shareholder and Beneficial Ownership List (Declaración Jurada de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March; confirms ownership as of 31 December of the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or discrepancies trigger fines up to US$5,000, suspension of e-Tax services, and loss of annual good-standing certification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Inactive Company Declaration (Declaración de Empresa Inactiva)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March; required for companies with no Panama-source business activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may cause the DGI to classify the company as active, imposing estimated income tax assessments, penalties, and removal from the inactive tax registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Confirmation to Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (file held at registered office; available for inspection by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero – UAF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual by 31 March, and within 30 days of any share transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain updated UBO information is an offence under Law 23 of 2015; penalties may be imposed on the company and the agent, and the company may be denied certification of good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent licensed audit is mandatory when annual gross income exceeds US$1,500,000 or year-end total assets exceed US$3,000,000; international interest entities and regulated activities face stricter thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Panama (NIIF); IFRS for SMEs is allowed for entities without public accountability.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any share transfer must be recorded in the share ledger, reflected in the board minutes, and notified to the resident agent for UBO register update within 30 days. The annual sworn shareholder list filed with the DGI constitutes the annual UBO confirmation for non-active companies.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial income tax system; foreign-source income (including revenue from offshore video matching subscriptions and cross-border telephony) is exempt from corporate income tax. Panamanian-source revenue is taxed at a flat 25%, subject to specific incentives: (i) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime – 0% tax on foreign-source income and full credit on certain local-source income; (ii) Colon Free Zone and special economic zones – reduced rates; (iii) film, tourism, and reforestation deductions. No general patent box or R&D super-deduction is available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 200 (Declaración de Renta – Personas Jurídicas); filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal (Sistema de Transmisión Electrónica de Formularios – STX) at www.dgi.gob.pa
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year entities, the return and payment are due no later than March 15 of the following year; an extension of up to two months may be requested from the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), legal name, fiscal year, and activities code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Panamanian RUC of the Sociedad Anónima; if no RUC has been issued, the foreign shareholder must apply through a local registered agent and include the fiscal year-end date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenues generated from operations, customers, or users located within the Republic of Panama
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue derived from Panamanian subscribers or in-country services; all foreign, non-Panamanian app-store and Paymentwall receipts must be allocated here if the video-matching service is delivered and consumed in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income sourced wholly outside Panama and thus exempt under the territorial regime
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full value of foreign IAP and Paymentwall collections in this box. A supporting schedule must detail the country-by-country origin of the users.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, including rent, salaries, depreciation, royalties, and third-party service fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses directly attributable to Panamanian-source income are deductible. Expenses allocated to foreign revenue must be pro-rated. Do not claim deductions for amounts paid to tax-haven shell companies without economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Excess of Panamanian-source gross income over deductible expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Box 103 exceeds Box 102, ensure no carryforward of losses from foreign activities is used to reduce Panamanian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax due on the net taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies that operate without a permanent establishment in Panama and have only foreign-source income will show zero here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments (anticipos), withholding tax credits, and any tax credits granted by DGI
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach copies of payment receipts. A company with no Panamanian-source income may apply for a refund or carry forward the creditable balance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 108 – Final tax due or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of tax due after prepayments or amount to be credited/refunded
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the balance in Balboas (USD) to the Banco Nacional de Panamá or through the DGI e-Tax gateway. Keep proof of payment for audit purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of a month, up to a maximum of 50%. If no tax is due, a fixed fine of B/.50.00. Non-filing or under-declaration: an additional 10% surcharge and monthly interest at the Banco Nacional rate. Criminal penalties for willful omission can reach 5 to 10 years' imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (standard rate on dividends paid out of profits derived from Panamanian-source income; no WHT on dividends paid from foreign-source income accumulated before repatriation).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce the 10% Panamanian dividend WHT, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence that has effective DTA, (ii) present the TRC and supporting form (Form 200 special annex or DGI Form 01-WHT) to the DGI prior to payment, and (iii) provide the company with a letter of beneficial ownership. The DGI issues an adjudication; a mere claim after the dividend payment is generally not accepted. Panama applies BEAT under DTAs. In the absence of a DTA, the 10% rate is final.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory domestic WHT of 10% for use of IP in Panama; treaty rates may reduce to 0-10%. Interest: statutory rate is 5% on interest paid to non-resident banks and 10% on other non-residents; interest paid on registered local foreign loans is exempt. Treaty relief follows the TRC protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory when annual related-party transaction volume exceeds B/.5 million (Panamanian Balboas, 1:1 USD), or when the taxpayer's total gross revenue exceeds B/.5 million and it engages in controlled transactions. A simplified Transfer Pricing Declaration (Form 200 annex) is required above B/.5 million; full contemporaneous documentation is required for intra-group licensing, app-store commissions, and service fees.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: While Panama has not adopted EU/Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), the DGI and the SEM law require economic substance for tax residence and treaty benefits. A Sociedad Anónima selling a link-only video match app must maintain: a physical office or registered agent with factual activity, local board minutes, a Panamanian bank account, and records showing effective management and control. Failure to demonstrate substance will lead to reclassification as a tax dominus of the shareholders' foreign income and can void transactionality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company assigns Panamanian-source subscription revenue to an offshore shell company or files a nil return without reporting in-country video-match users or local payment collections; intentionally omitting invoices from Paymentwall traceable to Panamanian traffic.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Surcharge of 100% on the evaded tax, interest at the Banco Nacional rate, seizure of bank accounts, and criminal fine equivalent to 2 to 5 times the tax evaded. Criminal imprisonment of 5 to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are personally liable for the full tax liability if they signed a knowingly false return; civil restitution, travel bans (impedimento de salida), and up to 10 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Panamanian S.A. is used solely to hold the Apple IAP account, register the app, and wire profits to a foreign beneficiary, while no actual board decisions, employees, or operational premises exist in Panama, and the company fails to file any return for three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may nullify the transfer of tax residence and treat all worldwide revenue as Panamanian-source, imposing 25% tax on gross receipts without deductions; administrative fine up to B/.100,000; cancellation of the corporate registration (matrícula) by the Registro Público.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The registered agent may be struck off; directors face personal joinder for the corporate tax debt, disqualification from holding a position in Panama-based companies for 5 years, and potential criminal sanctions for operating an undeclared exercise of commerce.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The video-match app collects payments through third-party rails (Apple IAP, Paymentwall) and does not file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) despite repeated high-value deposits from Brazilian, Russian, and UAE users; no KYC verification of users is conducted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015, fines from 100,000 to 5,000,000 Balboas per violation; dismantling of the legal entity if used for money laundering; up to 12 years' imprisonment for directors who knowingly fail to report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for AML fines; freezing of personal assets; travel bans; extradition may be sought by foreign jurisdictions for connected fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company declares dividends to non-resident shareholders from Panama-source profits without effecting the 10% WHT, or pays management fees to a related offshore entity at 20% markup without preparing a TP file though the threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding failure: 10% surcharge on the unpaid WHT plus interest back to the payment date; no offset credit to the shareholder. Transfer pricing: DGI adjusts the taxable base and imposes a 25% tax on the undeclared margin, plus a penalty of 50% of the additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who caused the corporation to declare dividends without WHT are jointly liable for the unpaid WHT; audit findings can be converted into criminal tax evasion proceedings; personal bank guarantees and judicial mortgages may be imposed.
